title: eval-harness: enhance prompt-set quality gating and CI hooks
author: Diego Morales
description: Motivation: Improve guardrails around prompt-set regressions and surface richer per-prompt metrics in CI. Summary: Adds a new prompt-quality gating rule, extends the eval-harness CI hook to emit per-prompt precision/recall/F1 metrics, improves failure messages with actionable links to the failing prompt-set and historical comparisons, and makes the GitHub Action run faster by parallelizing dataset partition evaluation. This PR implements: 1) prompt_quality_gate config with thresholds and severity mapping, 2) a new ci hook script (scripts/ci/prompt_quality_hook.py) that uploads per-prompt metrics to internal metrics endpoint and returns a structured exit code, 3) GitHub Action changes to run eval partitions in parallel and to cache model artifacts between runs, 4) tests and fixtures for edge cases (empty prompts, non-deterministic model seeds), 5) documentation updates to the eval-harness README and CI integration guide. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-5421) - [x] Unit tests for hook - [x] End-to-end CI smoke run - [x] Docs updated - [x] Performance run (parallelization) Related: replaces parts of ENG-5123 where earlier gating was too coarse. Rollout plan: feature flag enabled for canary CI runs for two weeks, then flip to default on main after a clean signal from nightly runs. Backward compatibility: hook is opt-in via repo config; existing repos without prompt_quality_gate will be unaffected. Why this matters: previous incidents (see incident docket SUP-112) surfaced regressions that were only visible at per-prompt granularity; these changes lower the signal-to-noise and make it actionable for engineers.
